source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the most characteristic symptom of hypertension, when present?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is often silent; when symptoms occur, headache on waking is most typical, plus dizziness, epistaxis, blurred vision.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Hypertension (PDF p. 113)
questions.quote: The most characteristic clinical manifestation of hypertension is headache especially upon waking.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: About what share of hypertension cases are essential (primary)?
questions.rationale: Essential hypertension of unknown cause makes up about 90%; secondary (renal, endocrine) about 10%.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Hypertension (PDF p. 112)
questions.quote: Essential hypertension is the most common type, affecting 90% of persons with high blood pressure.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which organs are the main 'targets' damaged by long-standing hypertension?
questions.rationale: End-target organs: heart (MI), brain (stroke), kidneys (renal failure), eyes (retinopathy) and peripheral vessels.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Effects of hypertension (PDF p. 113)
questions.quote: the end- target organs — brain, heart, kidneys, eyes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on hydrochlorothiazide should be monitored for which lab changes?
questions.rationale: Thiazides cause hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia and hypercalcemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Thiazide diuretics (PDF p. 114)
questions.quote: Electrolyte imbalance (hypokalemia, hypercalcemia, hypomagnesemia, and bicarbonate loss) Hyperglycemia Hyperuricemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is IV furosemide pushed slowly?
questions.rationale: Rapid IV furosemide can cause ototoxicity; urine output should rise within minutes.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Loop diuretics (PDF p. 116)
questions.quote: Administer IV Furosemide slowly; hearing loss may occur if rapidly injected.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before giving furosemide, the nurse asks about allergy to:
questions.rationale: Furosemide is contraindicated in hypersensitivity to sulfonamides.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Loop diuretics (PDF p. 115)
questions.quote: Furosemide is contraindicated if the client has hypersensitivity to sulfonamides.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client gains 1 kg overnight. The nurse estimates retention of about:
questions.rationale: A weight gain of about 1 kg (2.2 lb) reflects about 1 L of retained fluid.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Nursing interventions in diuretics (PDF p. 115)
questions.quote: A weight gain of 2.2 to 2.5 lbs. is equivalent to an excess liter of body fluids.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which combination increases the risk of hyperkalemia?
questions.rationale: ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics both raise potassium; avoid combining or monitor closely.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Potassium-sparing diuretics (PDF p. 117)
questions.quote: Spironolactone, Amiloride and Triamterene should not be taken with ACE inhibitors because they can also increase serum potassium levels.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on enalapril develops a persistent dry cough. The nurse recognizes this as:
questions.rationale: Dry cough is a common ACE-inhibitor side effect; ARBs do not usually cause it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 ACE inhibitors (PDF p. 121)
questions.quote: Side effects and adverse reactions (ACE Inhibitors) - Cough

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on an ACE inhibitor has swelling of the lips and tongue. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Angioedema is a life-threatening ACE-inhibitor reaction; stop the drug and protect the airway.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 ACE inhibitors (PDF p. 122)
questions.quote: Captopril may cause life — threatening effects: acute renal failure, bronchospasm, angioedema, agranulocytosis.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.stem: Which antihypertensive class is contraindicated in pregnancy?
questions.rationale: ACE inhibitors reduce placental blood flow and harm the fetus; methyldopa and labetalol are used in pregnancy.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 ACE inhibitors (PDF p. 121)
questions.quote: ACE inhibitors should not be given during pregnancy because they reduce placental blood flow.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on amlodipine reports swollen ankles. The nurse knows this is:
questions.rationale: Calcium channel blockers often cause flushing, headache, dizziness and ankle edema.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Calcium channel blockers (PDF p. 123)
questions.quote: Ankle edema

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on clonidine wants to stop it suddenly. The nurse warns this can cause:
questions.rationale: Centrally acting sympatholytics like clonidine must be tapered to avoid rebound hypertension.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Centrally acting sympatholytics (PDF p. 118)
questions.quote: to prevent rebound hypertension upon discontinuing drug therapy

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Hydralazine is often given with a beta-blocker to counter:
questions.rationale: Direct vasodilators drop BP and trigger reflex tachycardia; beta-blockers slow the heart.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Direct-acting vasodilators (PDF p. 120)
questions.quote: Beta — blockers are frequently prescribed with arteriolar vasodilators to decrease the heart rate

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client starting prazosin should be told to take the first dose at bedtime because of:
questions.rationale: Alpha-blockers cause dizziness and fainting from postural hypotension, especially early on.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Alpha-adrenergic blockers (PDF p. 119)
questions.quote: Dizziness - Faintness Lightheadedness

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on atorvastatin reports muscle pain and weakness. The nurse should:
questions.rationale: Statins can cause rhabdomyolysis and hepatotoxicity; muscle pain must be reported.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Antilipemics (PDF p. 126)
questions.quote: Muscle weakness and tenderness may be caused by rhabdomyolysis, and should be reported to the physician.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Leg pain that comes with walking and goes away with rest is called:
questions.rationale: Claudication is ischemic pain on activity relieved by rest, typical of arterial disease.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Arterial disorders (PDF p. 124)
questions.quote: Intermittent claudication. This is leg pain on activity and exercise, relieved by rest.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For a client with peripheral arterial disease, how should the legs be positioned?
questions.rationale: Slight dependency promotes arterial flow; elevation worsens arterial ischemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Arterial nursing interventions (PDF p. 127)
questions.quote: Place legs in slight dependency (lower than level of heart) to promote arterial flow.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which foot-care teaching is correct for a client with arterial insufficiency?
options: Use a heating pad on the feet
questions.rationale: Reduced sensation risks unnoticed injury; avoid barefoot walking and direct heat, cut nails straight, seek care for corns.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Preventing injury (PDF p. 129)
questions.quote: Do not go barefooted.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding suggests an abdominal aortic aneurysm?
questions.rationale: AAA presents with a pulsatile abdominal mass and back or flank pain; rupture causes shock.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Aneurysm (PDF p. 129)
questions.quote: Pulsatile mass over the abdomen.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which factor most increases the risk that an aortic aneurysm will rupture?
questions.rationale: Hypertension is the most common cause of aneurysm and raises the risk of rupture.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Aneurysm (PDF p. 129)
questions.quote: The most common cause of aneurysm is hypertension.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A woman with Raynaud's disease should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Avoid cold, stress, smoking and vasoconstrictors (e.g., ergots, oral contraceptives).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Raynaud's disease (PDF p. 130)
questions.quote: Wear gloves when handling frozen foods.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is part of Virchow's triad for DVT?
questions.rationale: Virchow's triad: vessel wall injury, venous stasis and hypercoagulability.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Deep vein thrombosis (PDF p. 131)
questions.quote: Venous stasis (e.g. prolonged bedrest)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is DVT considered potentially life-threatening?
questions.rationale: A dislodged deep vein clot can travel to the lungs as a pulmonary embolus.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Deep vein thrombosis (PDF p. 131)
questions.quote: DVT is potentially life — threatening because it may lead to pulmonary embolism.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which drug reverses bleeding from thrombolytic therapy?
questions.rationale: Aminocaproic acid (Amicar) is the antidote for thrombolytic-induced hemorrhage.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Thrombolytics (PDF p. 132)
questions.quote: Hemorrhage (antidote is Amicar / Aminocaproic acid)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on heparin has a falling platelet count. The nurse recognizes that heparin can cause:
questions.rationale: Heparin can decrease platelet count (heparin-induced thrombocytopenia); report it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Heparin (PDF p. 132)
questions.quote: It can decrease the platelet count, causing thrombocytopenia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: When should compression stockings be put on?
options: In the morning before getting up
questions.rationale: Apply before rising, when veins are least distended; turn them inside out to ease application.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 DVT nursing interventions (PDF p. 133)
questions.quote: It is applied before getting out of bed in the morning.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After vein ligation and stripping, the priority is to prevent:
questions.rationale: The priority after vein surgery is preventing thrombophlebitis; early ambulation helps.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Varicose veins (PDF p. 134)
questions.quote: Early ambulation prevents thrombophlebitis.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Buerger's disease is most strongly linked to:
questions.rationale: Thromboangiitis obliterans affects small and medium arteries, veins and nerves, mostly in male smokers; stopping smoking is essential.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Buerger's disease (PDF p. 134)
questions.quote: Most common etiologic factor is cigarette smoking.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which leg finding suggests venous rather than arterial disease?
questions.rationale: Venous: edema, brown pigmentation, warm skin, ankle ulcers, pulses present; arterial: pallor, hair loss, weak pulses, toe ulcers.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 5 Arterial vs. venous (PDF p. 134)
questions.quote: Ulcers occur in ankles
